arif.r1: Great question! Start at Masmak Fortress in the morning — it's where the story of modern Riyadh begins. Then walk to Murabba Palace and the National Museum next door.
arif.r2: For lunch, try a traditional Najdi dish like jareesh or kabsa near Al-Murabba. In the late afternoon, Diriyah's At-Turaif district is beautiful as the sun goes down.
arif.r3: I can turn this into a plan you can save. Just say “make it a plan” in the chat and I'll prepare the stops with times.

roaya.r1: Happy to help! For a calm day, begin at the National Museum while it's quiet, then take a long lunch break before heading to Al-Bujairi Terrace in the evening.
roaya.r2: At Expo 2030 I'd group the AI and technology pavilions together, so you walk less and have time for the live demonstrations.
roaya.r3: Would you like me to add a rest break between stops? It keeps the day relaxed, especially with family.

masmak.name: Masmak Fortress
masmak.description: A clay and mud-brick fortress, best known as the site of King Abdulaziz's recapture of Riyadh in 1902.
masmak.t1: Look for the spearhead in the old wooden gate.

murabba.name: Murabba Palace
murabba.description: King Abdulaziz's palace and seat of government, built in traditional Najdi mud-brick style in the 1930s.
murabba.t1: The upper floor shows original decorated ceilings.
murabba.t2: Photography is allowed in most rooms.

lunch.name: Lunch break
lunch.description: A rest and a traditional Najdi meal — try jareesh or kabsa. Suggested 60 minutes.
lunch.t1: Optional: shift it earlier or later to fit your pace.
lunch.t2: Many places close briefly for prayer times.

museum.name: National Museum
museum.description: The story of the Arabian Peninsula from prehistoric times to the unification of the Kingdom.
museum.t1: Start with the ancient Arabian kingdoms gallery.

turaif.name: At-Turaif District
turaif.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the birthplace of the first Saudi state, with restored mud-brick palaces.
turaif.t1: Golden hour light is beautiful on the walls.
turaif.t2: Wear comfortable shoes — paths are uneven.

bujairi.name: Al-Bujairi Terrace
bujairi.description: End the day at the dining terrace overlooking At-Turaif.
bujairi.t2: The view of the lit-up district starts at sunset.

voiceMode.title: Voice conversation mode
voiceMode.description: A dedicated voice experience for Arif and Roaya, opened from the chat. Speech is the device's own (demo); answers are simulated. Every state below is also reachable live.
voiceMode.servicesNote: “Live browser” uses your real microphone and device voices where supported. The simulations let you review the experience on any device.
voiceMode.sampleHeard: What should I see first in Riyadh?

limitationNotes.l1: Speech recognition depends on the browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari). Firefox has none; the mic explains this.
limitationNotes.l2: Chrome and Edge send recorded audio to their own recognition service. Morshid stores nothing.
limitationNotes.l3: The voice is the device's text-to-speech, so quality and Arabic availability vary. It is never presented as Arif's or Roaya's own voice.
limitationNotes.l4: Browser speech gives no audio levels, so the speaking animation is a gentle rhythm, not a true waveform. Listening uses real microphone levels.
limitationNotes.l5: Answers are simulated in this demo. The real assistant plugs into the same conversation loop later.

cardsAvatars.description: Card types with a clear hierarchy (eyebrow → title → description → meta → actions), consistent 16px radius and spacing, and restrained states. Avatars keep the original artwork with a size for every context.

notes.n1: Stops are compact by default; tap one to see its context, tips and actions.
notes.n2: “Edit itinerary” shows reorder arrows and remove buttons. Numbers, times, connectors, the summary and the route map update instantly.
notes.n3: Removing a stop shows Undo instead of a confirmation dialog.
notes.n4: “Save to My Plans” is the only way the proposal becomes a plan. Saving twice never creates a duplicate.
notes.n5: Saving is simulated (demo) and kept in this session only.

voice.capabilities: What works today and what needs a backend

capabilityNotes.c1: Works locally, free: microphone recording, waveform and cancel use standard browser APIs.
capabilityNotes.c2: Speech-to-text uses the browser's built-in recognition (Chrome, Edge, Safari). Some browsers, e.g. Chrome, send the audio to their own speech service to transcribe it; Morshid stores nothing.
capabilityNotes.c3: Read-aloud uses the device's text-to-speech voices — free, offline where the device has local voices.
capabilityNotes.c4: Arif's and Roaya's own voices, consistent Arabic quality on every device, and recognition on unsupported browsers need a future speech backend (behind the same interfaces).
capabilityNotes.c5: No paid APIs or keys are used. Audio is never recorded in the background — only after a tap.
capabilityNotes.c6: Firefox has no speech recognition: the mic explains this instead of failing.

rules.b1: Esc closes any dialog, sheet, menu, popover or place card.
rules.b2: Focus moves into the overlay when it opens and returns to the control that opened it when it closes.
rules.b3: Dialogs and sheets keep focus inside until they close.
rules.b4: Clicking outside closes menus, popovers and sheets; delete confirmations close only through their buttons or Esc.
rules.b5: Every overlay has a visible ✕ or Cancel, labelled for screen readers.
rules.b6: Overlays never exceed the screen: dialogs scroll inside, sheets stop at 90% height.
rules.b7: Bottom sheets keep their main actions in a fixed footer above the phone's safe area.
rules.b8: Sides follow reading direction: “start” panels open from the right in Arabic and from the left in English.

tell.body: In your own words, in Arabic or English: interests, time, pace and who is with you. Or pick one of the suggested questions.
tell.tip: Vague is fine — “something calm with my kids” is a good start.

suggest.title: Get personalised suggestions from your guide
suggest.body: Arif or Roaya suggest places with the reason they fit, and you can ask about any of them.
suggest.tip: In this demo replies are prepared from the guide data, not a live AI service.

build.title: Build and refine your itinerary
build.body: A proposal arrives as a plan you review: remove stops, reorder them, adjust times — then save it to My Plans.
build.tip: Nothing is saved until you choose to save it.

map.title: Explore destinations using maps
map.body: See your stops on a real map, look around for nearby places, or switch to the separate Expo preview map.
map.tip: Locations are verified; the Expo map is illustrative and says so.

manage.title: Manage your trip as you go
manage.body: Guided mode shows one stop at a time, with directions in Google Maps when you want them. You mark each stop done.
manage.tip: MORSHID never tracks you or assumes you've arrived.

tell.prompt: “A calm family afternoon in Riyadh — the kids love history.”

account.a: No. You can try the demo or continue as a guest. Saving some things asks you to sign in with a demo account — any email and an 8+ character password; nothing leaves your browser.

cost.a: No. The plans and credits you see in the demo are simulated, and there are no payments.

ai.a: Not yet in this demo: replies are prepared from MORSHID's guide data. A live AI service is planned.

location.a: No. Your position is only used once when you press “Where am I?”, and you mark stops as done yourself.

expo.a: No. It is an illustrative preview. Take Expo 2030 details only from official Expo 2030 Riyadh channels.

data.a: In this browser's local storage on your device. Clearing this site's data removes it.
